2.note: In Hebrew, they introduced speech by using two similar phrases. If this kind of repetition would not be natural in your language, you could combine them. Alternate translation: [Say to the sons of Israel]
Here, **sons of Israel** refers to the entire Israelite people, not just the male descendants or the original 12 sons of Jacob. Alternate translation: [the people of Israel] or [the Israelites]

Here, **a man** refers to any person, not a specific man. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Anyone] or [Any person]

This is a common expression meaning to make a special kind of vow. Your language may have a comparable expression that you can use in your translation, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [he makes a special vow] or [he makes a solemn promise]

The phrase **your valuation** occurs 19 times in the chapter. For people, the valuation is set here by Yahweh. For more information see the introduction to [chapter 5](ta:05) and how you translated this in 5:15. Alternate translation: [by the valuation of persons that I, Yahweh, give you]

3.q: מִ⁠בֶּן֙ עֶשְׂרִ֣ים שָׁנָ֔ה וְ⁠עַ֖ד בֶּן־שִׁשִּׁ֣ים שָׁנָ֑ה
3.note: Here, **son of** is a common expression in the culture which refers to a person who has some characteristic. In this instance, it is referring to males who have age ranges from 20–59. If this would be helpful to your readers, you could use an equivalent expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from age twenty to age fifty-nine]

In ancient times the silver **shekel of the holy place** was the standard weight kept by the priests in the Dwelling and later the temple. Alternate translation: [according to the standard shekel kept at the holy place]

4.note: The ages from verse 3, (twenty to fifty-nine years) carry over to this verse. You could include this information if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And if it is a female between twenty and fifty-nine years old]

5.note: This is a common expression referring to ages 5–19. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an equivalent expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from age five to age nineteen]

6.note: This is a common expression referring to ages one month to four years. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an equivalent expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from one month old to four years old]

7.note: This is a common expression referring to ages sixty and older. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an equivalent expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [sixty years old and older]

8.note: Here **too poor from your valuation** means unable to pay the standard amount. You could make this explicit in your translation if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And if he is too poor to pay the standard valuation]

Here, **he** refers to the person making the vow (who is poor), and **him** refers to the person that has been promised to Yahweh that the vower is trying to redeem. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [then the person making the vow shall present the one promised to Yahweh]

Here, **before the face of the priest** represents being in front of the priest. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [in front of the priest] or [in the priest’s presence]

This is a common expression meaning according to what someone can pay. If this phrase does not have that meaning in your language, you could use a comparable expression that does have that meaning, or you could state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [Based on how much the one making the vow can afford]

9.q: וְ⁠אִם־בְּהֵמָ֔ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יַקְרִ֧יבוּ מִמֶּ֛⁠נָּה קָרְבָּ֖ן לַֽ⁠יהוָ֑ה
9.note: The meaning of this verse may be unclear due to its complex structure. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation, if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [And if someone is presenting a portion of an animal as an offering to Yahweh]

10.note: The words **exchange** and **substitute** mean very similar things and are used together for emphasis. If your language would not use two similar words this way, you could combine them into a single clear expression. Alternate translation: [He must not trade it for another animal]

Some words are left out that in many languages a sentence would need in order to be complete. You could supply these words from the context if it would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [not a good animal for a worse one or a bad animal for a better one]

This Hebrew expression uses repetition of the verb “substitute” to intensify the idea. If your language does not repeat words for intensification, you could have another way of expressing the same idea. Alternate translation: [And if indeed he substitutes]

11.note: Here, **to the face of** represents being in front of the person. If it would be helpful in your language, you could use an equivalent expression or plain language. Alternate translation: [in front of the priest] or [in the priest’s presence]

12.note: Here, **your valuation** refers to the value that the priest determines for the poor person’s offering. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [The value that you, the priest, determine]

13.note: This Hebrew expression **redeeming he will redeem it** uses repetition to intensify expression of the idea. If your language does not repeat words for intensification, you could express this idea in another way. Alternate translation: [indeed he redeems it]
See how you translated this in 5:16.

14.note: Here, **a man** refers to any person, not a specific man. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could use an expression that would be more natural in your language. Alternate translation: [Anyone] or [Any person]

The phrase **between good and between bad** means the priest will assess the condition of the house to determine its value. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [according to the condition of the house]

15.note: In the phrase **the one consecrating**, the words “his house” are left out but understood from the previous verse. You could supply these words if it would be clearer in your language. Alternate translation: [the one consecrating his house]
See how you translated this in 27:13.

Here, **and it will be to him** is a common expression meaning that ownership will be transferred to him. You could use a comparable expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will belong to him]

Here, **your valuation** refers to the value that the priest determined based on the condition of the house. You could say that explicitly if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [the value you determined]

16.note: The phrase **field of his possession** refers to inherited property that was originally given to Israelite families when they entered Canaan. This property generally returned to the family every 49 years at Jubilee. Alternate translation: [from his inherited field]

This means the amount of seed. It could mean either (1) the amount of seed needed to plant the field or (2) the amount of seed the field produces. Alternate translation: [according to how much seed it takes to plant] or [according to how much seed to produce]

A **homer** was a unit of volume that may have been about 220 liters. If it would be helpful to your readers, you could express this in terms of modern measurement. Alternate translation: [about 220 liters of]

18.note: The phrase **upon the mouth of the years** is a common expression meaning based on the number of years. You could use a comparable expression from your language that has the same meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [according to the number of years]

19.note: The phrase **redeeming he will redeem** uses repetition to intensify the idea. If your language does not use repetition for intensification, you could use another way that is natural in your language to convey this meaning. Alternate translation: [if indeed he redeems]
See how you translated this in 27:13.

The phrase **it will stand to him** is a common expression meaning ownership will revert to him. You could use a comparable expression from your language that has the same meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [and it will belong to him again]

20.note: This verse presents a case where someone tries to profit twice from the same field by dedicating it and then selling it. As a result, they lose the right to the field permanently. You could say this explicitly if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [he will permanently lose the right to redeem it]

The expression **it shall not be redeemed again** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express this in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one will be able to redeem it again]

21.note: This is a common expression referring to when property ownership changes at the Year of Jubilee. You could use a natural expression in your language that has the same meaning or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [when ownership transfers in the Year of Jubilee]

A **field of devotion** refers to land that is completely and permanently dedicated to Yahweh. This is a stronger term than “consecrated.” You could use a term in your language that communicates this permanent, irrevocable dedication. Alternate translation: [as a field permanently and completely given to Yahweh]

22.note: The phrase **a field of his purchase** refers to a field someone has bought rather than inherited. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [a field that he has purchased]

A **field of possession** refers to inherited land that was originally given to Israelite families. You could state this explicitly if it would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [which is not part of his inherited family land]

24.note: Here both instances of **him** refer to the original owner who has inheritance rights, while **he** refers to the person who bought and then dedicated the field. It may be helpful to clarify this for your readers. Alternate translation: [to the original owner from whom the buyer bought it, to whom]

This refers to the person who permanently owns the land through inheritance rights. You could say this explicitly, if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [to the one who permanently owns the land by inheritance]

25.note: See how you translated this in 27:3.
A **gerah** was a unit of weight equal to about one-half gram. You could use a known unit of weight in your language. Alternate translation: [units each equal to about one-half gram]

26.q: בְּכ֞וֹר אֲשֶׁר־יְבֻכַּ֤ר לַֽ⁠יהוָה֙ בִּ⁠בְהֵמָ֔ה לֹֽא־יַקְדִּ֥ישׁ אִ֖ישׁ אֹת֑⁠וֹ אִם־שׁ֣וֹר אִם־שֶׂ֔ה לַֽ⁠יהוָ֖ה הֽוּא
26.note: The assumption is that readers will know that Yahweh automatically owns all firstborn animals from the time of the Passover, so no one can consecrate them. You could say that explicitly if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [no one may consecrate a firstborn animal to Yahweh, whether ox or sheep, because all firstborn animals already belong to Yahweh]

27.note: See how you translated this in 27:13

The phrase **if it is not redeemed, then it shall be sold** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [And if no one redeems it, then you must sell it at the value you determined]

28.note: A **devoted thing** refers to something that is completely and permanently dedicated to Yahweh. This is a stronger term than “consecrated.” See how you translated this in 27:21. Alternate translation: [thing permanently and completely given to Yahweh]

This refers to anything someone might own that could be devoted to Yahweh. You could indicate this explicitly in your translation if that would be helpful to your readers. Alternate translation: [whether a person, an animal, or an inherited field]
See how you translated this in 2:3.

29.note: All **devoted ones** refers to someone who is completely and permanently dedicated to Yahweh. When someone is **devoted to destruction**, it means they must be executed because they are enemies of Israel or have severely broken Yahweh’s covenant. Alternate translation: [people who must be executed because they are permanently condemned]

If your language does not use a passive verbal form in this way, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [All those whom Yahweh has condemned to death]

The expression **shall not be ransomed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use this form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [no one may pay to save their lives]

The expression **he shall be put to death** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use that form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [you must certainly execute them]

30.note: Here, **seed** represents all food crops that grow from seeds. If it would be helpful in your translation, you could use an equivalent expression or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [from the crops of the land] or [from what grows in the fields]

31.note: See how you translated a similar phrase about redeeming property in 27:19. Alternate translation: [indeed someone redeems part of his tithe]

32.note: This is a common expression that refers to how shepherds would count their animals by making them pass under a rod one by one. You could use a comparable expression from your language or state the meaning plainly. Alternate translation: [all that is counted in the flock]

33.q: לֹ֧א יְבַקֵּ֛ר בֵּֽין־ט֥וֹב לָ⁠רַ֖ע וְ⁠לֹ֣א יְמִירֶ֑⁠נּוּ
33.note: See how you translated this in 27:10. Alternate translation: [He must not inspect them to trade a good one for a bad one]

The phrase **It shall not be redeemed** is a passive verbal form. If your language would not use this form, you could express the idea in active form or in another way that is natural in your language. Alternate translation: [No one may redeem it]
